title: fix(marker-helpers): flag bad watermark fields, accept supersedes None
body:
<!-- idd-skill-authoring-publication: target=target-df9a1e8098f2ad28; anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#3334; set=set-1f543710dea874e1; session=session-f8e667821de4fb17; token=token-f330bb48e0eec96f -->

Parent roadmap: #3334

## Background

Two operational markers pass the shape check in
`src/scripts/marker-helpers.mts` but are then dropped by a stricter
parser or comparison, with no malformed signal (citations at
`fa49fb6c`).

**Review watermark: shape accepted, parse rejected, reported as
missing.** The `<!-- review-watermark:` entry in `OPERATIONAL_MARKERS`
(around lines 341-346) uses `\S+` for every field, so a body with a
short head SHA or a non-ISO timestamp is a recognized operational marker.
`parseReviewWatermarkComment` (around line 2979) then returns `null` for
it, because it requires `[0-9a-f]{40}` for the SHA and
`isValidIsoTimestamp` for both time fields. The malformed signal #2251
wired into F2 cannot see this case: `detectMalformedOperationalMarker`
(around line 3188) returns `null` as soon as `operationalMarkerPrefix`
matches, so `detectMalformedReviewWatermarkComments` in
`src/scripts/protocol-helpers.mts` (around line 5575) reports nothing
and `buildPreMergeReadinessSummary` falls through to
`{ route: 'return-to-e1', reason: 'missing-watermark' }` (around line
9410) instead of `'malformed-watermark'`. An agent that posted a
watermark with a typo is told it posted none.

**Claim marker: `supersedes: None` parses but never activates.** The
`claimed-by` grammar is case-insensitive (`/i`, around line 319), and
`parseClaimComment` (around line 929) returns the `supersedes` token
verbatim. `applyClaimEvent` in `protocol-helpers.mts` (around line
10652) accepts a fresh claim only when `claim.supersedes === 'none'`, so
a trusted, otherwise well-formed claim with `supersedes: None` or
`NONE` is silently ignored and is not reported as malformed either.
`renderClaimedByMarker` already normalizes case variants to `none` and
its comment (around lines 2537-2541) names this exact gap for emitted
markers; hand-composed markers still hit it. #1693 fixed the same class
for the watermark SHA by lowercasing on parse; the external-check-waiver
`none` sentinel is also compared case-insensitively
(`protocol-helpers.mts`, around line 997).

Out of scope: the forced-handoff marker's leading-whitespace tolerance
(`^\s*<!--` in its `OPERATIONAL_MARKERS` entry and `trimStart()` in
`parseForcedHandoffComment`). It is intentional -- commit `0d6ad23a`
("normalize forced handoff marker whitespace") added it on purpose so
audit and claim-resolution paths classify the same comments, and
`tests/forced-handoff-marker.test.mts` pins it
(`forced handoff parsing accepts leading whitespace before marker`) --
and the byte-0 anti-spoofing note on `detectMalformedOperationalMarker`
covers only markers that carry a `malformedPrefixPattern`, which the
forced-handoff entry does not.

## Proposed change

1. Make `detectMalformedReviewWatermarkComments` also report a trusted
   comment whose `operationalMarkerPrefix` is `<!-- review-watermark:`
   but which `parseReviewWatermarkComment` rejects, keeping the existing
   `expectedClaimId` scoping. Leave the shape pattern itself
   unchanged, so such a body stays excluded from the review-activity
   universe exactly as today.
2. In `parseClaimComment`, normalize a case-variant `none` in the
   `supersedes` slot to `none`, mirroring `renderClaimedByMarker`; real
   claim IDs pass through verbatim.
3. Add regression tests for both.

## Acceptance criteria

- `node --test tests/pre-merge-readiness.test.mts` passes with cases
  asserting `reviewCurrency.comparisonReason` is `'malformed-watermark'`
  for a trusted watermark whose head SHA is 12 hex characters and for
  one whose `maxActivityUpdatedAt` is neither an ISO timestamp nor `none`, and stays
  `'missing-watermark'` when no watermark-shaped comment exists.
- `node --test tests/review-gate.test.mts` passes with a case asserting
  `detectMalformedReviewWatermarkComments` still ignores a field-invalid
  watermark whose claim ID differs from a supplied `expectedClaimId`.
- `node --test tests/protocol-helpers.test.mts` passes with a case
  asserting `resolveActiveClaim` returns an active claim for a trusted
  first claim marker carrying `supersedes: None` and one carrying
  `supersedes: NONE`, and `parseClaimComment` returns `supersedes` as
  `'none'` for both.
- `pnpm run build:check` passes.

## Candidate files

- `src/scripts/protocol-helpers.mts`
- `scripts/protocol-helpers.mjs`
- `src/scripts/marker-helpers.mts`
- `scripts/marker-helpers.mjs`
- `tests/pre-merge-readiness.test.mts`
- `tests/review-gate.test.mts`
- `tests/protocol-helpers.test.mts`

---

fixes with exact expected outputs._
